summary: President Donald Trump approved new tariffs of up to 30% on imported solar equipment, significantly impacting the $28 billion renewable energy industry that relies heavily on foreign parts. This decision, aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing, is expected to increase costs for solar projects and could lead to job losses, though some analysts believe the impact might be less severe than anticipated. title: APS, First Solar plan large West Valley solar power plant with giant battery
summary: First Solar Inc. and Arizona Public Service Co. (APS) are partnering to build a large solar power plant in the West Valley, Arizona, featuring a massive battery storage system. This project is unique for its battery size and operational strategy, designed to deliver electricity specifically during peak demand hours (3-8 p.m.). The plant aims to address the "duck curve" problem associated with increased solar integration on the grid by charging batteries during off-peak hours or selling excess solar energy, and then supplying APS when demand is highest.

title: UPS, Workhorse team up to develop all-electric Class 5 truck
summary: UPS is partnering with Workhorse Group to develop all-electric Class 5 delivery trucks, with an initial deployment of 50 vehicles for real-world testing. These trucks are expected to offer a nearly 400 percent fuel efficiency improvement and a 100-mile range. This initiative is part of UPS's broader strategy to electrify its fleet, building on existing electric and hybrid vehicles and recent orders for Tesla Semi tractors and Fuso eCanter trucks.

title: 10 Best and Worst Safety Options
summary: This article evaluates various safety options available in modern cars, categorizing them into best and worst based on their effectiveness and value. It highlights essential features like forward collision warning with automated braking and backup cameras, while also critiquing less effective or inconsistent systems such as some blind spot monitoring and lane departure warning systems. The author uses their experience and data from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety to inform their recommendations.

title: Axon CEO may make $1 billion in the next 10 years or nothing at all, but he's excited for the challenge
summary: Axon CEO and co-founder Rick Smith's new performance plan is modeled after Tesla CEO Elon Musk's compensation plan, offering him the potential to earn $1 billion over the next decade or nothing at all. This ambitious compensation structure highlights a significant shift in executive incentives, directly tying leadership wealth to long-term company performance. The plan reflects a growing trend of incentivizing high-risk, high-reward leadership in the tech industry.

title: For backup power, batteries join the mix as prices come down
summary: Home battery systems are becoming a more affordable and popular alternative to traditional generators for backup power, especially in areas prone to storm outages. Sunrun Inc. has introduced its Brightbox system in Massachusetts at a competitive price, aiming to capitalize on consumer demand for reliable, clean backup energy. Other companies like Tesla are also expanding their home battery offerings as costs decline and incentives grow.

title: Musk’s $2.6 billion award cheered on by big Tesla shareholders
summary: Two of Tesla Inc.'s largest shareholders, Baillie Gifford & Co. and T. Rowe Price Group Inc., are supporting a plan to award Elon Musk a compensation package valued at $2.6 billion. This backing comes despite proxy adviser Glass Lewis & Co. recommending against the plan due to potential shareholder dilution. The shareholders believe Musk's vision is crucial for Tesla's continued growth not just in automotive but also in energy markets.

title: Electric dreams: Lucid Air
summary: The Lucid Air is an all-electric luxury sedan developed using a largely digital design and engineering process. The article highlights the collaborative approach between design and engineering teams, the significant reliance on digital tools like Autodesk Alias and VRED, and the extensive use of multiphysics simulation for optimizing the vehicle's components and overall performance. Despite a rapid two-year development cycle and lacking traditional automotive heritage, Lucid Motors aims to break free from conventional car design, focusing on maximizing occupant space and delivering cutting-edge technology.

title: Faraday Future May Be Planning China Production Line for Its First Electric Car
summary: Faraday Future, led by Jia Yueting, appears to be planning a production line for its FF91 electric car in China. An affiliate company, Ruichi Smart Car Guangzhou Co., has been established with registration details matching requirements for an NEV production site recently auctioned in Guangzhou. This move could significantly cut costs for the FF91, the world's most expensive NEV.

title: Ford, Once a Leader in the S.U.V. Race, Aims to Catch Up (Published 2018)
summary: Ford Motor, once a leader in the SUV market, is now making a concerted effort to regain its position by introducing numerous new SUV models over the next three years. The company plans to make SUVs and pickup trucks account for 90 percent of its North American vehicle production by 2020, with a focus on hybrid, electric, and off-road variants. Ford also aims to cut costs by streamlining vehicle development and reducing the number of basic component architectures.

title: Uber Crash Is Nightmare Driverless World Feared but Expected
summary: A self-driving Uber test car struck and killed a pedestrian in Tempe, Arizona, on March 18, raising significant concerns about consumer confidence in autonomous vehicle technology. This incident, the first known fatality involving an autonomous test vehicle and a pedestrian, is prompting investigations and a call to slow down the industry's rapid march toward commercialization, especially in contrast to a previous Tesla fatality which involved a driver using an assistance system. The event is expected to have a broader impact on the future development and regulation of fully autonomous driving systems.

title: Texas DMV seeks to clarify dealership law — as it tries to enforce it

The proposed changes, which could impact these cases, aim to define "own" more precisely and limit prohibitions to manufacturers owning dealerships that sell their specific products. This initiative comes amidst pushback from the Texas Automobile Dealers Association, which has different stances on the enforcement against Berkshire Hathaway and Cummins, and highlights the contentious nature of current regulations for companies like Tesla Inc.

title: FedEx Reserves 20 Tesla Semi Electric Trucks
summary: FedEx Corp. announced it has reserved 20 Tesla Semi electric trucks, which are slated for production in 2019 and will be operated by FedEx Freight. This investment highlights FedEx's commitment to sustainability, improving road safety, and reducing its environmental impact. The Tesla Semi trucks are expected to offer advanced safety features and significant energy cost savings compared to diesel trucks.

summary: Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang argues that autonomous vehicle development, particularly in safety, must continue and investments should increase despite a recent fatal accident involving an Uber self-driving car. Nvidia itself temporarily halted its AV testing to assess new data but continues development using simulators.
